subject: Follow-up: post-discovery model fit & prompt collection
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Meera Shah <meera@curahealth.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.k@curahealth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap + ask: prompt capture & redaction checklist

Hi Meera / Samir —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and a concrete ask to help accelerate model fit evaluation:

- Use case: clinical documentation summarization and triage (physician notes -> structured summary + risk flags).
- Data characteristics: free-text clinical notes, occasional scanned text, some inconsistent templates; estimated scale ~50–80 req/s during peak.
- SLOs & metrics: 95% useful-summary rate (customer feedback), P95 latency target ~200 ms, token-cost sensitivity.
- Constraints: PHI in text (we discussed minimal retention for POC), strict audit trail for flagged items.

What we need to move to a short POC (4 weeks):
1) A set of ~200 real anonymized prompts/samples and ~50 edge-case examples (examples of truncated notes, shorthand, misspellings, mixed languages). If you can, drop them into the Drive folder below. If you prefer, reply with a ZIP or CSV.
2) Redaction guidance from your team: which PHI elements you are comfortable removing vs. keeping context for model evaluation. We can provide a checklist template.
3) A prioritized success criteria list (e.g., specific downstream checks we should run during evaluation).

I've attached a prompt-capture template to make uploads straightforward and a short PDF with initial model recommendations based on today's pattern. Monica (cc'd) will follow up with concrete model/benchmark pointers and a checklist for safe sample sharing.

Attachments: [curahealth_prompt_template.csv], [redwood_model_recs.pdf]

Drive upload link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDefG-prompt-uploads
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/CH-2027-57

Next step: if you can confirm by Tue (2/16) that you'll share the sample set, we'll queue an SE-led evaluation and a short benchmark run against 3 candidate configurations.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Hi Aditya —

Appreciate the clear recap. We can get the sample bundle together but a couple quick clarifying questions before we upload:

- For anonymization, are you ok if we run a first-pass redaction on identifiers (names, MRNs) but keep relative temporal info ("3 days ago") and clinical abbreviations?
- For edge cases: we have a handful of voice-to-text transcriptions with sentence breaks missing — should those be in the same CSV or a separate file?
- Who on Redwood will handle the SOC2/logging conversation? We need to confirm retention and access controls for any logs generated during the POC.

Timeline: we'll aim to anonymize and share a 100–150 sample subset by EOD Wed (2/17). The rest (up to 200) will follow the week after.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Discovery recap + ask: prompt capture & redaction checklist

Hi Meera / Samir —

Great to meet you today (and thanks Aditya for the intro). I pulled together an initial set of concrete recommendations for the POC and a short redaction checklist you can apply before uploading samples. See below.

Model & eval recommendations (initial shortlist)
- config A: rwd-13b-v2-quant — best balance of cost and accuracy for summarization; good for on-prem/dedicated.
- config B: rwd-70b-optim — higher-quality summaries for complex notes (higher cost).
- config C: rwd-13b-llama-compat-8bit — low-cost baseline for throughput testing.

Benchmarks we'll run (examples)
- ROUGE-1/2/L and clinical concept F1 on labeled subset (~300 tokens scale)
- P95 latency at batch sizes aligned with your traffic pattern (we'll simulate 60 req/s peak)
- Regression test against your prioritized prompt list (we'll run the current production heuristic baseline if you provide it)

Prompt capture guidance (use this CSV schema)
- columns: sample_id, raw_text, context_notes, expected_summary, priority_label (high/med/low), edgecase_flag, redaction_applied (yes/no)
- Please separate voice-to-text transcripts into a column named transcription_source. If many broken sentence boundaries, mark edgecase_flag=true.

Redaction checklist (recommendation)
- Required: remove direct identifiers (full names, MRNs, SSNs). Replace with placeholders like [NAME], [MRN].
- Recommended: remove free-text addresses and phone numbers. Keep age ranges and relative dates ("2 weeks ago") if useful for clinical context.
- Optional: for category-level testing, provide an additional column with masked tokens preserved (e.g., [AGE:42]).
- Note: if you want us to run the POC with unredacted samples in a private deployment, we can discuss an on-prem or VPC deployment and a KMS/HSM key option.

Attachment: sample_prompts_redaction_examples.csv (contains a few redacted examples + edge-case rows).
Drive: same upload folder — I'll create a subfolder /curahealth_poc/samples and share permissions to meera@curahealth.ai.
Security & logs: our Security team will follow up on retention — short answer: for hosted POC we can enable a non-persistent logs mode and provide audit export; for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention to your policy. I'll loop in security if needed after you send samples.

Let me know if you'd like a short video walkthrough of the CSV template — happy to record a 7-min screencast.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
